bibliography: Corpuz, M. N. C., Paller, V. G. V., & Ocampo, P. P. (2016). Diversity and distribution of freshwater fish assemblages in Lake Taal river systems in Batangas, Philippines. Journal of Environmental Science and Management, 19(1), 85-95.

primarySource.title: Diversity and distribution of freshwater fish assemblages in Lake Taal river systems in Batangas, Philippines

accessReview.repositoryMetadata: Official UKDR metadata page and its abstract reviewed.
accessReview.publisherFullText: Official UPLB journal PDF text was available to the web research viewer and reviewed for methods and study-level results.
accessReview.localAcquisition: A direct local request to the publisher PDF returned HTTP 403; no local binary was retained.

survey.subject: Freshwater fish assemblages in the Lake Taal river systems: Looc and Magapi inlet rivers and Pansipit outlet river.
survey.designAsReported: The article says 12 stations were selected among three river sites, with a 60-75 m reach at each station and three 20-25 m runs treated as within-station replicates. It separately reports 48 samples as 24 sampling sites multiplied by two seasons; the station/run/sample denominators are not reconciled in the text reviewed.
survey.seasonLabelConflict: The abstract maps July to wet season and January to dry season. The methods sentence maps January and July to wet and dry, respectively, which reverses that assignment; the same methods section describes Batangas dry months as November-May and wet months as June-October. No season-specific assignment is adopted here.
survey.identification: Captured fish were counted and identified to the lowest possible taxon; the paper says some voucher specimens were deposited at the UPLB Museum of Natural History, without catalog identifiers in the reviewed passages.
survey.locality: The article describes Pansipit as Lake Taal outlet and its only drainage, approximately 9 km long, draining to Balayan Bay. No exact station-coordinate list or station-to-estuary crosswalk is transcribed or inferred.

reportedRichness.abstract: The UKDR abstract reports 37 species across the three rivers and 36 species in Pansipit; it reports 21 each for Looc and Magapi.
reportedRichness.overallIndividualCountConflict: The UKDR abstract reports 3,342 individuals while the article results text reports 3,346. The total is not adopted.
reportedRichness.interpretation: Historical, study-defined river richness from the 2011 survey only. It is not a current-presence estimate, a complete present-day inventory, or 36 estuary species.

rightsReview.policyFinding: The UKDR JESAM policy states that authors assign article copyright to UKDR and lists limited personal-use exceptions. Reproduction, transmission, distribution or use of article material outside those exceptions requires a written agreement and attribution to UKDR.
rightsReview.decision: Keep the species-by-river/season table and feeding-habit entries untranscribed pending written permission or a verified applicable license. A free-to-read PDF is not treated as a reuse license.

waterbodyAttribution.riverEvidence: The article explicitly treats Pansipit as the outlet river and reports its aggregate richness separately from Looc and Magapi.
waterbodyAttribution.estuaryEvidence: No station is assigned to the separately modeled Pansipit River Estuary. Do not transfer the Pansipit river aggregate or any river table row to the estuary.
waterbodyAttribution.geometry: No channel or estuary geometry added; the article narrative and study map are not adopted as a verified GIS boundary.

nextActions: Seek written permission from the UKDR/JESAM rights holder or locate a separately licensed, station-resolved source before transcribing the species-by-site table or feeding-habit column.
If rights are cleared, independently check source-spelled taxa and resolve any taxonomic synonyms; retain field-identification and voucher limits.
Obtain the station map/coordinates and a documented river-versus-estuary crosswalk before assigning any station result to the estuary; do not infer channel geometry from the article map.
Keep all findings historical to the 2011 survey and do not use them for current presence, absence, diet or bait recommendations.
